title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Scope of Authority of Entrusted Agents in Civil Litigation in Enforcement Procedures

articles.content_en:
Supreme People's Court
Reply on the Issue of the Scope of Authority of Authorized Agents in Civil Actions
During Enforcement Proceedings
Fa Fu [1997] No. 1
Shanxi Higher People's Court:
Your court's Shan Gao Fa [1996] No. 78 "Request for Instructions on Whether the Scope of Authority of Authorized Agents in Litigation Includes Enforcement Proceedings" has been received. Upon study, the reply is as follows:
According to the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, a party in a civil action may appoint an authorized agent. When a party appoints an authorized agent, it shall submit to the People's Court a power of attorney that clearly states the entrusted matters and the specific scope of authority of the agent, in accordance with law. If the party fails to specify in the power of attorney that the agent has authority in the enforcement proceedings and the specific matters of agency, the agent shall have no authority in the enforcement proceedings and may not directly receive or dispose of the subject matter on behalf of the party.
Hereby this reply.
January 23, 1997
